title: Hotel reservation lifecycle
idea: A reservation's lifecycle is a state machine: seven statuses, a fixed set of allowed moves, and date guards that refuse moves at the wrong time.
points: HELD becomes CONFIRMED on payment, EXPIRED at the deadline, or CANCELLED on decline.
CONFIRMED moves to CHECKED_IN, CANCELLED, or NO_SHOW after the check-in date.
CHECKED_OUT, CANCELLED, EXPIRED and NO_SHOW are terminal: nothing leaves them.
Every move asks the enum first, then checks the date guard.

messages.label: hold(DLX, 10-13 Mar)
messages.note: The guest picks a room type and dates. A Reservation is created in HELD.

messages.label: reserve(3 nights)
messages.note: One Deluxe unit is taken on each of the three nights, or none.

messages.label: RS-1 HELD, 15 min
messages.note: The guest gets a deadline. If it passes, the system moves RS-1 to EXPIRED.

messages.label: confirm(RS-1, token)
messages.note: The guest pays inside the deadline.

messages.label: charge(total)
messages.note: The service charges the held total once.

messages.label: ok
messages.note: Payment succeeded: HELD moves to CONFIRMED. A decline moves it to CANCELLED and frees the nights.

messages.label: checkIn(RS-1, room 201)
messages.note: On 10 March the desk assigns a real Room. CONFIRMED moves to CHECKED_IN.

messages.label: checkOut(RS-1)
messages.note: On 13 March the guest leaves. CHECKED_IN moves to CHECKED_OUT, a terminal state.

code.title: Status enum with guards
code.caption: Allowed moves live in the enum; date guards live in Reservation. Wrong moves are refused and reported.

walk.text: RS-1 takes the happy path, but first tries to check in a day early.
RS-2 never arrives, then a late check-in is attempted.
RS-3 expires, then a payment arrives for it anyway.
`next()` lists the allowed next statuses; terminal ones return an empty set.
First guard: is this move in the enum's allowed set at all?
Date guards: no check-in before the date, no no-show until the day has passed.
Report and stop on refusal; otherwise print the move and change status.

pitfalls: Do not set `status` directly from controllers; every change must go through `move`.
Treat a late payment for an EXPIRED hold as a refund case, never a confirm.
Mark NO_SHOW only after the check-in day ends, in the hotel's own time zone.

quiz.q: What does ReservationLifecycle print for RS-2's check-in?
options: RS-2 refused NO_SHOW -> CHECKED_IN (before check-in date)
quiz.why: RS-2 is already NO_SHOW, a terminal status. Its `next()` set is empty, so the first guard refuses before any date check runs.

takeaway: Statuses change only through allowed moves, each checked against the calendar.

starters: What should happen when a NO_SHOW guest turns up the next morning?
Should early check-in be a separate status or just a guard?
Where does the job that expires HELD reservations run?
